title: Experiment design: constant fan-in DST (MethodX)
method: MethodX: sparse-to-sparse dynamic sparse training with a constant fan-in constraint (every active neuron has exactly k incoming weights). Every ΔT steps, per layer: count each neuron's salient weights (layer top-K by weight or by gradient magnitude), ablate neurons with fewer than γ_sal·k salient weights (floor of one) and give their budget to the rest, recompute k′, prune the K smallest-magnitude weights layer-wide, and regrow each active neuron by gradient magnitude up to fan-in k′. ERK (or uniform) layer densities, sparse fan-in-scaled init, update fraction α cosine-decayed to zero at an end fraction, then the mask is frozen. Inference uses a condensed n_active × k values + indices representation with CPU and GPU kernels; a closed-form variance analysis of the output-norm ratio motivates the constraint.

compute.hardware: One to four V100/A100-class GPUs per training run; latency on a Xeon-class workstation CPU and a Volta-generation GPU

claims.text: MethodX learns constant fan-in fine-grained structured sparsity with fully sparse-to-sparse training, and its generalization matches state-of-the-art unstructured DST up to very high sparsity across image-classification architectures
At very high sparsity unstructured DST implicitly ablates whole neurons; a strict constant fan-in constraint prevents this, and dynamic neuron ablation restores unstructured-level accuracy
Neuron ablation can be enabled at all sparsity levels; the resulting width sparsity complements constant fan-in sparsity for real-world inference speed while keeping generalization
The condensed constant fan-in representation is parameter- and memory-efficient and gives real speedups for batch-1 CPU and batched GPU inference versus dense and unstructured sparse representations
Constant fan-in does not impair training dynamics: its output-norm variance is no larger than unstructured sparsity, especially at high sparsity

questions.text: At matched global sparsity, layer-wise distribution, update schedule and training budget, does enforcing constant fan-in (with dynamic neuron ablation) during sparse-to-sparse training lose generalization relative to unstructured DST? (99% is pre-registered as exploratory)
questions.hypothesis: For ResNet-class image classifiers at 80, 90, 95 and 99% global sparsity, MethodX with neuron ablation reaches top-1 test accuracy within δ of RigL trained under the identical configuration, checked on the lower end of a 95% CI on the mean difference across seeds
questions.predictionIfFalse: At any sparsity ≤ 95%, the CI on (MethodX − RigL) falls entirely below −δ
questions.minEffect: δ = 0.5 pp on CIFAR, 1.0 pp on ImageNet (proposed; to be confirmed by the user before any run)

questions.text: Implicit ablation: percentage of neurons with zero fan-in at the end of training, per layer, and the strict vs ablation accuracy gap (RigL vs MethodX-strict vs MethodX+ablation)
Ablation at all sparsities: accuracy and final layer widths with ablation on vs off (same setup as the primary comparison)
Inference speed and memory: condensed vs dense vs CSR/unstructured kernel vs structured-only (narrower dense), same trained weights, same threads
Does the closed-form variance of ‖z^{l+1}‖²/‖z^l‖² match Monte Carlo under Bernoulli, exact-count and constant fan-in masks?
questions.hypothesis: Each closed form matches simulation within MC error, and Var(constant fan-in) ≤ Var(Bernoulli) everywhere

methodComponents.name: constant fan-in constraint (exactly k incoming weights per active neuron)
dynamic neuron ablation (γ_sal saliency threshold, budget redistributed)
saliency count: union of layer top-K by weight and top-K by gradient magnitude
ablation threshold floor of one salient weight
recompute constant fan-in k′ from surviving neurons
layer-wide pruning of the K smallest-magnitude weights
per-neuron regrowth by gradient magnitude up to fan-in k′
dense-gradient accumulation over mini-batches for regrowth
connectivity update schedule (ΔT, α cosine-decayed to the update-end fraction, then mask frozen)
initialization scaled by the sparse fan-in
set of sparsified layers (first layer, attention projections)
equal numbers of weights pruned and regrown
condensed inference representation (values + indices; ablated neurons deleted; can run as narrower dense)
compiled CPU implementation and GPU kernels for constant fan-in layers
